label: UniFi U6 Mesh
description: Wi-Fi 6 mesh access point: 4x4 5 GHz plus 2x2 2.4 GHz, meshing on the 5 GHz client radio because there is no dedicated backhaul radio. Single GbE RJ45 uplink fed by 802.3af PoE (12.95 W), IPX5 housing for indoor/outdoor mounting.

label: UniFi U6 In-Wall
description: In-wall Wi-Fi 6 AP (4x4 5 GHz + 2x2 2.4 GHz, no dedicated backhaul radio) with a built-in 4-port GbE switch: one data-in GbE uplink plus four data-out GbE ports, one of which can pass 802.3af PoE through. Powered by 802.3at PoE+ (25.5 W, required for the PoE output).

label: eero Pro 6E
description: Wi-Fi 6E tri-band mesh router, 2x2 on 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz (AXE5400 class); the 6 GHz band carries both clients and mesh traffic, so there is no dedicated backhaul radio. Two auto-sensing ports per unit, one 2.5GbE and one 1GbE, so a 2.5G wired backhaul is possible on the primary node.

label: Google Nest Wifi Pro
description: Wi-Fi 6E tri-band mesh unit (AXE5400, 2x2 on 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz) where the 6 GHz band doubles as the mesh backhaul, with no dedicated backhaul radio. Two GbE ports per point for WAN/LAN, so wired backhaul tops out at 1G; the primary point routes with NAT/DHCP and there is no local web UI.

label: TP-Link Deco XE75
description: AXE5400 tri-band Wi-Fi 6E mesh: 2x2 on 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz, with the 6 GHz radio (radio2) used as the dedicated wireless backhaul between Deco units. Three GbE auto-sensing ports per unit, so wired backhaul is 1G only unless you step up to the XE75 Pro variant with its 2.5G port.

label: TP-Link Deco BE85
description: BE22000 tri-band Wi-Fi 7 mesh (2.4 GHz 1376, 5 GHz 8640, 6 GHz 11520 Mbps) that bonds all three bands with MLO instead of a separate backhaul radio. Two 10G ports (one RJ45, one Ethernet/fibre combo) plus two 2.5G ports per unit, any of which can carry 10G or 2.5G wired backhaul.

label: NETGEAR Orbi RBK852 (RBR850 + RBS850)
description: Orbi 850 tri-band Wi-Fi 6 mesh: 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz for clients plus a dedicated 5 GHz backhaul radio (radio2) linking router and satellites. The router has a 2.5Gbps Internet port and four GbE LAN, each satellite adds four more GbE LAN.

label: NETGEAR Orbi RBKE963 (RBRE960 + 2x RBSE960)
description: Orbi 960 quad-band Wi-Fi 6E (AXE11000): 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz serve clients while a fourth, dedicated 5 GHz radio (radio3) is the mesh backhaul to the satellites. The RBRE960 router has a 10G Internet port, one 2.5G LAN and three GbE LAN; each RBSE960 satellite has a 2.5G LAN port that can also take wired backhaul.

label: Linksys Velop MX5300 (MX5 Velop AX)
description: Velop MX5 tri-band Wi-Fi 6 (AX5300): a 2.4 GHz radio, a 4x4 5 GHz client radio at 2402 Mbps and a second 4x4 5 GHz radio at 1733 Mbps used as the mesh backhaul (radio2). Five GbE ports (one WAN, four LAN), all gigabit - this model has no 2.5G port.

label: ASUS ZenWiFi ET8 (AXE6600)
description: ZenWiFi ET8 AXE6600 tri-band Wi-Fi 6E mesh: 574 Mbps on 2.4 GHz, 1201 Mbps on 5 GHz and 4804 Mbps on 6 GHz, with the 6 GHz band usable as the dedicated wireless backhaul (radio2). One 2.5G WAN plus three GbE LAN per unit - the 2.5G port is the only multi-gig link and can be reassigned to LAN/backhaul.

label: Zyxel Multy M1 (WSM20)
description: Multy M1 AX1800 dual-band Wi-Fi 6 mesh node: 2x2 2.4 GHz at 574 Mbps and 2x2 5 GHz at 1201 Mbps, meshing on the 5 GHz client radio with no dedicated backhaul radio. Four GbE ports per unit (one WAN plus three LAN) and no multi-gig port.

label: TP-Link Deco P9 powerline mesh
description: AC1200 dual-band Wi-Fi 5 mesh with a HomePlug AV1000 powerline backhaul: units bridge over the mains wiring on plc0, so interior walls and distance do not cut the mesh. Two GbE auto-sensing ports per unit and no dedicated wireless backhaul radio.
